sentences.text: Mesetasaurus is known from two well-preserved tail vertebrae.
The fossils were discovered in the 1980s, and the species was formally described in 2026.

The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — consists of two tail vertebrae, likely the third and sixth in the series, found at the Meseta de Artigas locality. The specific name protector honors the Uruguayan hero José Gervasio Artigas.
Mesetasaurus is classified as an aeolosaurin titanosaurian sauropod belonging to the clade Aeolosaurini. Phylogenetic analysis places it deeply nested within this group.
Mesetasaurus lived in the Late Cretaceous (potentially Coniacian to Maastrichtian) in Uruguay.
The presence of Mesetasaurus supports a Coniacian to Maastrichtian age for the Guichón Formation, a view favored by researchers who found dinosaur eggshells similar to Sphaerovum there.
Some researchers have historically debated a Lower Cretaceous age for the Guichón Formation based on similarities with the Migues Formation.
